newsitem.title: USA: U.S. December T-bonds finish strongly higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. December T-bonds finish strongly higher.

text.p: U.S. December Treasury bond futures finished strongly higher, fueled early in the day by weak data and later by talk of benign inflation.

A weaker than forecast September National Association of Purchasing Managers index at 51.7 versus 52.6 in August sparked a buying wave early that pushed December even farther above key support. A drop in the BTM/Schroders U.S. weekly chain store sales index earlier in the day had also buoyed the market, traders said.
Volume tapered off at midday but rose later on talk that Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan was unconcerned about inflation.

Traders cited a report in the Australian Financial Review's Wednesday edition saying that Greenspan did not see inflation as an immediate risk to the United States. The report quoted Australian Treasurer Peter Costello as saying Greenspan was "very optimistic" in a meeting between the two.
"He indicated to me that he saw no threats to inflation down the track," the Review reported Costello saying.
Bullish traders embraced the talk and pushed December T-bonds above 110-00 resistance to set a fresh session high in the afternoon of 110-2/32.
Traders pegged resistance at 110-10/32, last Friday's high.

"This thing is really chugging," said Mike Boss, futures analyst with Aubrey G. Lanston. He pegged significant resistance at 112-00, the 38-percent retracement on weekly bar charts of the 95-00 to 122-00 move.
Traders said one firm was a seller of 3,000 December contracts in afternoon trading, forcing December T-bonds to close below their session highs. December T-bonds closed up 23/32 at 109-29/32.
One trader noted that 109-25/32 was a high volume area from last week and December could gravitate around that price as Friday's key employment data nears.
On Friday, September U.S. payroll data will be released. Non-farm payrolls were seen up 166,000 compared with a 250,000 gain in August.
March Euros finished up seven bps at 94.14 and March bills ended up seven at 94.68.
